## Open user decisions (not implemented; current behaviour kept and recorded)
- **D3-a** Verifier authentication in CI: pin the auditor to a user-named FPIA version. Today the PR CI runs the PR head's own `track_c_fpia*.py`; `runtime_provenance.verifier` records the commit and blobs only.
- **D3-b** Restore a content-independent job-id collision rule for spoof detection. Today a job id/name collision with the Track C workflow (e.g. `validate`) is a note (`job_id_collision_note`) on a real finding only; probe S17 is pinned as *not found*.
- **D3-c** Declare dynamically constructed invocations (string-built paths, paths in shell variables, importlib with computed names) a non-claim. Today they are not detected and the result says so: `integration_interference.dynamic_invocation_detection = NOT_CLAIMED` plus a constant non-claim; probes S15/S16 are pinned as *not found*.
- **D3-d** #28 attribution (`implementation/docs/codex_takeover/evidence/track_c/independent_c8_audit.py` is an unattributed importer of Track C modules; the T28 merge gives `FPIA_FAIL`). Unchanged; still FOUND.

### Interpretation note for G7 (pending the user's confirmation)
> `track-c-fpia.yml` now runs its audit job on `pull_request` only when the PR's base or head branch matches `integration/**` (PIW integration / trial merge results); other PRs get a skipped job, not a red check. `workflow_dispatch` is unchanged. This reflects the recommended interpretation **"FPIA applies to merge results containing R"**, pending the user's confirmation. It relabels nothing: a tree without R is still `authority FAIL` / `FPIA_FAIL` when audited.

### PyYAML packaging (why the head is `523e702`, not only `babf0a4`)
`babf0a4` pinned PyYAML 6.0.1 in `track-c-fpia.yml` and imported an installed PyYAML. On PR CI the six other `pull_request` workflows (p01-research-publication, qgv-invalidation-binding, sec-primary-disclosure, technical-real-model, technical-real-producer, us-equity-session) run the whole native suite with pytest and numpy only, and **60 FPIA tests failed there** (p01 job: 60 failed, 1710 passed; reproduced locally in a pytest+numpy venv: the same 60). The `track-c-fpia` audit of the same head passed. A concurrent writer of the same PIW session then pushed `523e702` (*vendor pure-Python PyYAML 6.0.1 so the FPIA tests run where PyYAML is not installed*): `_vendor/yaml` = `lib/yaml/*.py` of the upstream PyYAML-6.0.1 sdist byte for byte (sdist sha256 `bfdf460b...`, per-file digests in `_vendor/README.md`, `cyaml.py` left out), `track_c_fpia_workflows.py` imports only that copy, the install-step pin is removed, `test_integration_fpia_vendor.py` pins the files. This fix2 task had prepared an alternative follow-up (`118cb3c`: skip the YAML-dependent tests where PyYAML is absent, `FPIA_REQUIRE_YAML=1` in FPIA CI); it was **not pushed** because `523e702` had already landed and makes it redundant. Detection logic is unchanged by `523e702`.

## Contract
`python implementation/tools/integration/track_c_fpia.py --repo PATH --tree <T> --register-commit <G> --cdr CDR-014 --out FILE.json [--work-dir DIR] [--keep-work]`
`python implementation/tools/integration/track_c_fpia.py --verify-output FILE.json [--expect-result-sha256 <64-hex>]` (G4; exit 0 VERIFIED, 1 MISMATCH, 2 unreadable)

- `--repo` must be a complete, non-shallow repository; otherwise NOT_RUN. All git work runs in a sandbox populated by fsck-verified fetches whose status lines are parsed for refused ref updates (G3). Trees are materialised from raw blobs and verified.
- `--out` must be new or empty and `<out>.verbatim/` absent or empty (G4); otherwise `FPIA_NOT_RUN`, nothing written.

- No edit to any frozen tool (`track_c_c6_acceptance.py` a60c4c5f, `track_c_c7_acceptance.py` 6b9362d0, `track_c_c8_partial_acceptance.py` e587a8d5), Frozen record, approval record, owner or Codex branch, or PR #40; no history rewrite; no force-push.

Track C acceptance is not weakened: G1/G2 widen what is FOUND; G3 removes a false NOT_RUN only for ref names; G4 refuses instead of overwriting; G5/G6/F2 are normalisation, wording and disclosure; G7 changes only which PRs trigger the CI job.
- Open user decisions D3-a/b/c/d are not implemented (see above); D3-b and D3-c are pinned as current behaviour.
- No new numeric threshold, default or tolerance: every comparison is exact (self-test enforced). `timeout-minutes: 150` is a CI job limit, not an FPIA comparison.
- **No PR-specific or hard-coded SHA exceptions** in code, tests or the workflow (self-test scans all of them; 0 40-hex literals in the added lines).
